title: The independent reading of the law text captured by M4-T029 (lot lines, rear yards beyond the corner and for interior and through lots, ZR 23-436, ZR 34-21, special density areas, the base plane, eligible sites, 'residence, or residential'), written into the R6B reference cases - two independent readings from a sealed folder, a value only where both agree, every change with its reason (D-090 R226, R241, R259, R291, R318)
objective: Read independently the law text captured by task M4-T029 (27 texts), and write what the readings settle into the R6B reference cases (docs/plans/R6B_RESULTS_CONNECTION_WORK_ORDER_2026-10-06.md, section 8: 'capture the missing law text, then read it independently'; backlog row DB-170 item (a)). INPUT MADE BY THE ORCHESTRATOR BEFORE THE BUILDER STARTS: two readings by two different AI helpers that took no part in writing the program's rules, each working alone from a sealed folder (every pinned law capture without its notes, the benchmark lot's recorded official facts and outline, the made-up lots' dimensions, no program output) and with no access to the program or the repository. The readings cover: (1) the ZR 12-10 definitions of the lot lines, lot width and lot depth, applied to the benchmark lot and to a made-up interior lot; (2) the rear yard: the part of a corner lot beyond 100 feet of the corner point, the interior lot under ZR 23-342, and the through lot under the rear yard equivalent of ZR 23-343; (3) ZR 23-436 and what ZR 35-633 brings in for the benchmark lot; (4) ZR 34-21 and what stays open without ZR 34-22 and 34-23; (5) whether the benchmark lot is in the Manhattan Core or the Special Downtown Brooklyn District, from their definitions; (6) from what level heights are measured (the base plane) and which facts that needs; (7) to which zoning lots ZR 23-434 and the different maximum of ZR 23-362(b) apply; (8) the definition of 'residence, or residential' and what the captured allowance sections name as the base of a share of floor area. THE BUILDER then: saves the two returns unchanged under docs/reference-cases/R6B/provenance/; records a value or a yes/no only where BOTH readings give it on the same basis, and 'not known' with the reason and both readings named everywhere else; changes an existing row's expected value only where both readings support the change, with a dated change-log entry (corrected evidence: the text is now captured and read); says, in each row and in the README, 'the readers did not have' a text, never that the repository 'does not hold' it, and brings the case files' older 'not captured' and 'uncaptured' wording into that form where it touches a row it changes (the reviewer's standing observation in DB-170); updates the README; re-renders the pages; extends the test support only as the new rows need. Point (8) is recorded as a reading only: the measurement-basis record is NOT changed by this task. Nothing in a case comes from a program run. No rule file, rule engine, capture, register entry, plan or screen changes.
business_reason: Rows of the reference cases stay 'not known' for want of text that is now captured: the through-lot rear yard, what ZR 35-633 adds, the special density areas, the rear yard beyond the corner. Step 3 of the owner's eight steps (R291) and the owner's rule that interpretation is checked with independently worked, source-backed examples kept apart from program output (R226, R241, R259, R318). The engine work of Part 0 tests against these rows.
